steps.tx: **Sjogren disease** is a chronic systemic autoimmune exocrinopathy characterized by dense lymphocytic infiltration of salivary and lacrimal glands. Exocrine destruction results in classic sicca symptoms: **xerostomia** or dry mouth, and **keratoconjunctivitis sicca** or dry eyes, demonstrating a profound female preponderance of approximately 9 to 1.
steps.say: Sjogren disease is an autoimmune exocrinopathy causing lymphocytic infiltration of salivary and lacrimal glands. Patients present with dry eyes and dry mouth with marked female predominance.

vis.alt: Pathology of salivary and lacrimal gland infiltration in Sjogren syndrome
vis.caption: Lymphocytic infiltration causes acinar gland destruction and severe sicca symptoms. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: The **2016 ACR/EULAR classification criteria** apply to patients presenting with daily dry eye or dry mouth symptoms. The scoring system assigns **3 points** for focal lymphocytic sialadenitis with a focus score of 1 or more on minor salivary gland biopsy, and **3 points** for positive anti-SSA/Ro antibodies. A cumulative score of **4 or more points** confirms classification.
steps.say: The ACR and EULAR criteria require at least 4 points to classify Sjogren disease. Positive salivary biopsy focus score and positive anti-SSA Ro each contribute 3 points.

steps.tx: Definitive histopathologic confirmation relies on minor labial salivary gland biopsy. A positive diagnostic **focus score** requires the presence of at least **1 focus** containing **50 or more mononuclear inflammatory cells** per **4 square millimetres** of glandular tissue, predominantly composed of CD4 positive T helper cells and infiltrating B lymphocytes.
steps.say: Salivary gland biopsy evaluates focal lymphocytic infiltration. A positive focus score requires at least one aggregate of 50 mononuclear cells per 4 square millimeters.

nodes.label: Incisional labial minor salivary gland biopsy
Focus score >=1 aggregate of 50 mononuclear cells confirms Sjogren

steps.tx: Extraglandular manifestations involve multiple organ systems in up to 30 to 40 percent of patients. Common features include non-erosive inflammatory arthritis, interstitial lung disease, Raynaud phenomenon, and **type II mixed cryoglobulinemia**. Cutaneous involvement manifests as **palpable purpura** driven by cutaneous leukocytoclastic vasculitis.
steps.say: Extraglandular manifestations occur in up to 40 percent of Sjogren patients. Features include non-erosive arthritis, interstitial lung disease, and purpuric vasculitis.

rows: Sensory ganglionopathy and painful small fiber neuropathy
Abnormal skin biopsy epidermal nerve density

steps.tx: Renal involvement predominantly takes the form of chronic **tubulointerstitial nephritis**, leading to distal **type 1 renal tubular acidosis**. Impaired collecting duct hydrogen ion secretion causes hypokalemia, hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis, alkaline urine pH, medullary nephrocalcinosis, and recurrent hypokalemic periodic paralysis.
steps.say: Tubulointerstitial nephritis causes distal type 1 renal tubular acidosis. Impaired proton excretion leads to hypokalemia, alkaline urine pH, and nephrocalcinosis.

nodes.label: Distal intercalated cell proton pump failure
Type 1 RTA with hyperchloremic acidosis, hypokalemia, nephrocalcinosis

steps.tx: Patients with Sjogren disease carry an extraordinary **15- to 20-fold increased lifetime risk** of developing **non-Hodgkin B cell lymphoma**, predominantly **mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue** or MALT lymphoma of the parotid glands. Red flags include persistent painless parotid enlargement, low serum C4, monoclonal paraproteinemia, and cryoglobulins.
steps.say: Sjogren disease carries a 15- to 20-fold increased risk of non-Hodgkin B cell lymphoma, particularly MALT lymphoma. Persistent parotid swelling and low C4 are red flags.

vis.alt: MALT lymphoma risk and parotid gland monitoring in Sjogren syndrome
vis.caption: Chronic B-cell stimulation predisposes to marginal zone and MALT lymphomas. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.tx: Symptomatic treatment of sicca symptoms combines preservative-free artificial tears and oral secretagogues. Muscarinic agonists **pilocarpine at 5 mg three to four times daily** or **cevimeline at 30 mg three times daily** stimulate residual functional exocrine acini, relieving dry mouth and ocular grittiness.
steps.say: Secretagogues pilocarpine and cevimeline stimulate muscarinic receptors on residual salivary tissue. They effectively relieve distressing oral and ocular dryness.

left.title: Pilocarpine therapy
points: Dose 5 mg three to four times daily

right.title: Cevimeline therapy
points: Selective M1 and M3 muscarinic agonist
Fewer cardiac and bronchospastic side effects

steps.tx: Extraglandular systemic disease activity is quantified using the **EULAR Sjogren Syndrome Disease Activity Index** or ESSDAI across 12 organ domains. Mild articular symptoms respond to hydroxychloroquine, whereas severe cryoglobulinemic vasculitis, glomerulonephritis, or central neuropathy requires systemic glucocorticoids and B cell depletion with **rituximab**.
steps.say: The ESSDAI instrument scores systemic organ activity in Sjogren disease. Severe manifestations like cryoglobulinemic vasculitis require corticosteroids and rituximab.
